claim: Dorfman 1943 (pooled tests; independent items with one known failure rate p, a pool costing one test, a failed pool retested one by one): pooling k items costs 1/k + 1 - (1 - p)^k tests per item, so a pool saves tests when (1 - p)^k > 1/k, which holds below p = 0.307 for pools of 3, 0.293 for 2 or 4 and 0.243 for 7 (computed); a pool of 2 is never optimal (Aldridge and others 2019), and the best pool is 11 at 1 % failing (80 % saved), 4 at 10 % (41 %) and 3 at 30 % (1 %); not tested on our check, whose failures may not be independent and whose run over k changes may cost more than one run.

Untested decision rule, version 2 (decided 2026-11-19): at every start and finish of a unit of work, work out for each resource how many units it can carry now and run at the smallest, acting only at the gate (version 1's frame, kept); the resources are memory (the hard limit), processor, memory bandwidth, the check, ready work, the parent session's own window, and each token window (the 5-hour period, the week, on some plans a week for one model). Two stops: the least important unit when memory reaches its floor, and a unit that reaches its own cap commits what it has, hands the rest over through files and ends. A token window limits by fit, always (a unit starts only if its usage fits in what every window it draws on has left above the reserve, the reserve being the caps of the running units until usage per unit is measured), and by order when the waiting work is more than the window can pay for before its reset (the highest value per token first; with equal values the fewest expected tokens). Tokens are held back only as a reserved share for units that must not stall and for other clients on the same windows (no number yet) and, once units have values, by a price. Capping starts at (1 - u)/(1 - s) of the even rate from u > s is not adopted; it stays an arm of the pacing simulation (Q33).
when: Before deciding how many helpers, sessions or heavy commands to run at once, what to do when a job is slow, or whether to hold work back for a token window.
